title: Bucktown and joining the union as a cymbal player
summary: At Bruning's he got into the union at 16 or 17 on cymbals rather than trombone.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Oh yeah, that's how I got in the union.
It was a place called Bruning's and Martin's.
I think Martin's is still there, huh?

Well, my uncle owned that last. He sold it out before he died. He bought Martin out and it was called Brunus and Bruning's. No relations. Yeah. So Bruning wanted me. I sat in there one time and I was in the union. I was a punk kid. So Bruning's is, the drummer at Bruning's was the secretary of the union. He says, I want this boy in the union. He says, I want him to work here. So he put up the $50 and I went, I had to go down to the union for examination, you know. Yeah. So I went in on cymbals. What was that? To get in the union. So they put up the piano player when he tries out, he played, the number I know by backwards, they goes to the spirits of independence. I started doing it. He says, you're in, that's enough.
You got in as a cymbal player.
I couldn't get into reading a trombone.
Yeah, they'd make you read something.
They thought I was reading it.
Yeah. That's what I mean. For the trombone, they would have put up something.
That's what the drummer told me. He says, take the cymbals, it's easy.
So I made the introduction. Boom, boom, boom. Ching, boom, boom. Crazy.
How old were you then about when you got in the U?
